answer: In an agent marketplace for ocean freight, terrace repairs, and garden care, each identity must lock $100 of collateral for 90 days before it can bid on jobs. The lock applies to every account, so creating 10,000 fake agents ties up $1 million for three months. Splitting funds among aliases cannot increase the number of eligible bidders: each new identity requires another deposit, making a sybil swarm costly in both capital and lost interest.
